updated_claim: Thailand imported coal consumption (2023): 18.1 Mt total coal imported, of which 11.2 Mt consumed by the industrial sector (non-power manufacturing), 4.1 Mt by IPP power producers, and 2.8 Mt by small power producers (SPP, many of which are industrial co-generation). Additionally, 12.7 Mt of domestic lignite was consumed exclusively by EGAT (state power utility) at Mae Moh. The original ~11.2 Mt figure is confirmed for the 'Industry*' sector per EPPO classification, but the full picture is: total coal imports = 18.1 Mt, power sector coal (IPP) = 4.1 Mt, industrial coal = 11.2 Mt; with a further definitional question whether SPP (2.8 Mt) counts as industrial. Sub-bituminous coal (11.7 Mt of imports) originates predominantly from Indonesia; bituminous (6.0 Mt) from Australia and Russia. Thailand produces no commercial coal — all 18.1 Mt of coal is imported. Indonesia is dominant supplier of the sub-bituminous coal that industrial users prefer.

research_notes.original_claim_accuracy: The 11.2 Mt figure is precisely confirmed by EPPO Table 4.1-2 (Coal Industry* = 11214.010 thousand tons for 2023). The original Statista secondary source had the right number.
research_notes.critical_refinement: The claim omits that total coal consumption is 18.1 Mt (power + industry) and that an additional 12.7 Mt of DOMESTIC lignite goes to EGAT power. The '11.2 Mt industrial' is only the coal portion of industrial use; industrial also used 0.05 Mt lignite. SPP (2.78 Mt) is ambiguous — officially 'power producers' but many are industrial co-generation plants.
research_notes.import_origin: Indonesia confirmed dominant for sub-bituminous category (11.7 Mt of 18.1 Mt total imports). Bituminous (6.0 Mt) comes from Australia and Russia. No primary source with exact %-by-country for full year 2023 found, but Indonesia's dominance is unambiguous from the sub-bituminous category volume.
research_notes.all_imported_claim: CONFIRMED. EPPO T04_01_01 shows Thailand's only domestic coal is lignite from Mae Moh mine, 100% going to EGAT. There is no domestic commercial coal/bituminous mining. All 18.1 Mt of coal consumed was imported.
research_notes.sector_breakdown_for_industrial_boiler_c: The 11.2 Mt 'Industry' category is the most relevant figure for package boiler analysis. It excludes IPP power plants (dedicated coal power stations). SPP (2.78 Mt) is borderline — these are often sugar mills, paper mills, and cement co-gen plants that DO use package-type or industrial boilers.
research_notes.data_currency: EPPO tables confirmed updated April 2026, with 2023 marked as 'Preliminary' in footnote. Data sourced from Thailand Customs Department.
